l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: NSL Article 42(2) sets a no-bail-unless threshold for national security bail applications.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA statement of the statutory text used in construing NSL Article 42(2).

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: For NSL bail, Article 42(2) introduces a threshold materially more stringent than ordinary bail under the Criminal Procedure Ordinance.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA distinguishes the NSL Article 42 threshold from ordinary bail.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: NSL Article 42(2) operates as a specific exception within the existing bail regime, rather than replacing the whole bail regime.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA frames NSL Article 42(2) as a special threshold within the wider bail system.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: When assessing NSL Article 42(2), the court may consider whether bail conditions affect the future risk assessment.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA rejects a sealed-off first stage that excludes proposed bail conditions.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Appropriate bail conditions may be relevant to the risk assessment because they can deter breach or further offending.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA connects conditions to risk management and deterrence.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFA summarised NSL Article 42(2) as a specific exception importing a stringent threshold for bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFA summary of conclusions.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFA held that Tong (No 1) erred in a crucial respect by misapprehending the nature and effect of the NSL Article 42(2) threshold.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Lineage marker showing Lai limiting/correcting Tong on NSL bail threshold.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Tong treated Article 42(2) as targeting the risk of offending while on bail in respect of national security offences.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Earlier CFI treatment; must be read with later CFA correction in Lai Chee Ying.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Tong treated NSL Article 42 as emphasizing the weight to be given to risk of reoffending in NSL bail applications.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Earlier CFI application on Article 42 risk weighting; answer composers must show later CFA treatment in Lai Chee Ying.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Tong stated that Article 42 does not wholly shut out a defendant from applying for bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Earlier CFI statement; read with the CFA's later framing of Article 42 as a stringent threshold.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: In NSL bail review, the court's future-risk assessment is a judgment on what the accused may or may not do in the future.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Useful candidate paragraph on the predictive nature of bail risk assessment.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Tong refused bail on conventional grounds of flight risk and risk of reoffending.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal illustration; not answer-safe without review.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Ma treated an undertaking as a possible means, in an appropriate case, of satisfying the NSL Article 42(2) bail requirement.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI candidate application on undertakings; must be compared with factual refusal at paragraph 33 and later CFA treatment.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Ma illustrates that a proposed undertaking may fail to satisfy the bail court where the facts suggest the defendant may not abide by it.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive refusal despite proposed undertaking; useful as contrast to Lai CFI paragraph 33.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Ma recognises that prolonged pre-trial detention may eventually justify a renewed bail review depending on the later state of affairs.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate point on renewed review/new circumstances; not a general entitlement without factual review.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI in Lai treated NSL Article 42(2) as not being a categorical no-bail provision.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI statement later considered by the CFA in the same litigation; show with CFA Article 42 threshold propositions.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI in Lai accepted a case-specific undertaking and residence confinement as sufficient on the facts before it for the Article 42 future-risk assessment.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI bail-grant illustration later reviewed in CFA proceedings; candidate lineage only.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI in Lai stated that bail decisions are not final: bail can be revoked and refusal can be reopened on new circumstances.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate procedural point on bail review/revocation/new circumstances.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The post-CFA Lai bail review restated the NSL Article 42(2) no-bail-unless formulation.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI post-CFA restatement of Article 42(2); pair with CFA ratio propositions for answer hierarchy.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The post-CFA Lai bail review applied the CFA's formulation that NSL Article 42(2) imports a stringent threshold for bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of the CFA Article 42 threshold; CFA remains the controlling source.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: In applying the Article 42(2) threshold, the bail court may consider all apparently relevant materials, including proposed conditions and non-trial-admissible materials.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI post-CFA application of the factors/materials part of the Article 42 assessment.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The post-CFA Lai bail review emphasised that bail decisions involve a future-looking risk assessment.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate application point on forward-looking bail risk assessment.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Article 42(2) future-risk inquiry is not confined to repeating the charged conduct, but may extend to prohibited acts more broadly.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI application on scope of prohibited acts in future-risk assessment.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The post-CFA Lai bail review refused bail because the court was not satisfied that the Article 42(2) future-risk threshold was met.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal after applying the CFA Article 42 framework.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Chan Chi Chuen Raymond
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Chan applied the CFA formulation that NSL Article 42(2) imports a stringent threshold for bail applications.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of Lai CFA threshold in a later NSL bail review.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Chan Chi Chuen Raymond
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Chan applied the Article 42(2) approach that the bail court considers all relevant matters, including proposed conditions and non-trial-admissible materials.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI candidate application of the CFA factor/materials approach.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Chan Chi Chuen Raymond
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Chan illustrates that NSL bail assessment remains applicant-specific and requires consideration of the individual's circumstances.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate application point on individualised bail assessment.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Chan Chi Chuen Raymond
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Chan treated public-record matters, non-public assertions, past performance, conduct, and offered bail conditions as relevant to the predictive assessment.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate illustration of facts considered in the predictive and evaluative exercise.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Chan Chi Chuen Raymond
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Chan illustrates a case where conditions were treated as sufficient on the facts to satisfy the Article 42(2) future-risk threshold.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive grant illustration; not a general rule without review.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Chan Chi Chuen Raymond
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Chan illustrates that stringent conditions may address surrender-to-custody risk on the facts of a bail review.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive ordinary bail-risk illustration within NSL bail review.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fan Kwok Wai Gary
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Fan frames the NSL bail inquiry as requiring the applicant to overcome the first threshold laid down in Lai CFA.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate second-bail-application source using Lai CFA threshold terminology.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fan Kwok Wai Gary
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Fan treats long delay before trial as a relevant concern in a second NSL bail application, although not automatically decisive.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate delay/new-circumstances point for second bail applications.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fan Kwok Wai Gary
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Fan cites the need for proactive case management where a remanded NSL defendant remains in pre-trial custody for lengthy periods.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate pre-trial delay/case-management point; source quotes Ng Hau Yi Sidney through Fan.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fan Kwok Wai Gary
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Fan records that long wait for committal and trial may be raised as a fairness concern in a renewed bail application.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Candidate fairness/delay point; paragraph records submission and must be labelled carefully until reviewed.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fan Kwok Wai Gary
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Fan refused the second bail application because the applicant still had not overcome the first Article 42/Lai threshold.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive refusal on a second application; not a general rule.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Sze Tak Loy
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI applied Lai CFA as establishing that NSL Article 42(2) is a stringent threshold exception to ordinary bail principles.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of Lai CFA threshold; candidate only and subordinate to CFA ratio.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Sze Tak Loy
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Bail conditions may satisfy the ordinary second-threshold concern of surrendering to custody.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI application on surrender-risk conditions.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: In NSL bail applications, the CFI applied Lai CFA as permitting consideration of all relevant matters, including bail conditions and non-trial-admissible materials.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of the CFA all-relevant-materials approach.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: A predictive and evaluative assessment may lead to refusal where there are insufficient grounds to believe the applicant will not continue acts endangering national security.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal applying the NSL bail threshold.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Wan Siu Kin Andrew
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI characterised NSL bail assessment as a predictive and evaluative exercise on all materials before the court.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of predictive/evaluative assessment terminology.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Wan Siu Kin Andrew
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, absence of sufficient grounds under the NSL threshold led to refusal of bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal; candidate only.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Mo Man Ching Claudia
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI considered materials, submissions and proposed bail conditions in a predictive and evaluative NSL bail assessment, but refused bail where sufficient grounds were absent.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal after considering proposed conditions.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI applied Lai CFA by considering all relevant matters, including possible bail conditions and materials not admissible at trial.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of CFA all-relevant-materials approach.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, imposed bail conditions satisfied the court that the applicant would not continue NSL offences if granted bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI grant illustration; not a general rule without review.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Bail conditions may satisfy ordinary s.9G concerns about surrendering to custody or committing an offence while on bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI grant illustration on ordinary second threshold.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Wong Pik Wan
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI treated Lai CFA as establishing that NSL 42(2) creates a stringent threshold exception to ordinary bail principles.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of Lai CFA threshold formulation.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Wong Pik Wan
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI refused a prosecution review after finding insufficient grounds to believe the respondent would continue NSL acts if bailed.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive grant/continued-bail illustration following Lai CFA.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Or Yiu Lam Ricky

l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI found sufficient grounds under the NSL first threshold for the respondent not to continue NSL acts if granted bail.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive grant/continued-bail illustration following Lai CFA.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Or Yiu Lam Ricky
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Where both thresholds were satisfied on the facts, the CFI maintained bail on the Chief Magistrate’s terms.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI considered all materials, submissions and even potentially inadmissible materials in making the predictive NSL bail evaluation.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of all-relevant-materials approach following Lai CFA.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI refused bail because sufficient grounds under the NSL first threshold were absent.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: Fact-sensitive CFI refusal; candidate only.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI repeated that the NSL bail test requires a predictive and evaluative exercise.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of predictive/evaluative assessment terminology.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI was not satisfied that the applicant would not continue NSL-endangering acts if granted bail.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI restated that this form of NSL bail application requires a predictive and evaluative exercise.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of predictive/evaluative assessment terminology.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI considered the words used, circumstances, submissions and possible bail conditions in assessing future NSL risk.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of all-relevant-materials and possible-conditions approach.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fung Tat Chun Frankie

l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI described the sequence for NSL bail: first the Article 42 threshold, then the ordinary Criminal Procedure Ordinance threshold only if the first is satisfied.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Fung Tat Chun Frankie

l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, failure to overcome the first NSL threshold led to refusal of bail.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Tam Man Ho Jeremy Jansen

l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI found no sufficient grounds under the NSL first threshold and revoked bail.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Kwok Ka Ki

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI restated that NSL bail assessment requires a predictive and evaluative exercise.
l4_case_applications.lineage_note: CFI application of predictive/evaluative assessment terminology.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI considered proposed bail conditions but was not satisfied that the NSL first threshold was met.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, extra bail conditions satisfied the CFI that the respondent would not continue acts endangering national security.

l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Bail / NSL bail threshold and conditions
l4_case_applications.application_summary: After the NSL first threshold was passed, the CFI considered ordinary risks of reoffending, absconding and surrender to custody.

l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI applied Lai CFA as establishing the stringent NSL Article 42(2) bail threshold.

l4_case_applications.case_name: HKSAR v Ng Man Yee Carol

l4_case_applications.application_summary: On the facts, the CFI refused bail because it was not persuaded the applicant would not continue NSL-endangering acts.

l4_case_applications.application_summary: The CFI described NSL bail as involving a more stringent first-threshold inquiry into whether the accused will not continue NSL-endangering acts.
